elements.content: A JavaScript closure is created whenever a function is defined inside another function, allowing the inner function to access variables from the outer scope, even after the outer function has finished executing.

The Classic Encapsulation Pattern

JavaScript doesn't have native "private" modifiers for objects. Closures emulate this by locking variables inside a function scope, making them only accessible via explicitly returned privileged methods.

Function factories

Closures are widely used as "function factories" that pre-fill or cache certain arguments for future use, letting you dynamically create customized functions.

Memoization

Because closures retain access to variables in their outer scope even after execution, they are incredibly useful for caching expensive results and avoiding redundant calculations.
With great power, comes great responsibility

Memory Leaks

Closures can unintentionally hold large, unneeded objects in memory. Because the inner function maintains a reference to the outer scope, the Garbage Collector cannot clean up the outer variables for as long as the inner function is still reachable.

Loop Variables and the var Trap
Before ES6, declaring variables with var was a notorious source of bugs with loops and closures because var is not block-scoped. All iterations would reference the exact same variable memory slot.

What problem React solved

Before React:

  • * UI was manipulated directly through the DOM.
  • * Developers manually updated HTML when data changed.
  • * State was spread across many places.
  • * Complex UIs became difficult to maintain.
